method: Every drop is charged the average horizontal run plus the riser distance, and that figure is increased by the slack allowance: cable per drop = (average run + riser) x (1 + slack / 100). The job total is that figure multiplied by the number of drops, and the boxes to buy are the total divided by the box size rounded up to the next whole box, with a one-part-in-a-billion tolerance so a total that lands exactly on a full box is not rounded again. Box sizes are the international foot definition (0.3048 m), so the 1000 ft box is 304.8 m and the 500 ft box is 152.4 m, with a 500 m drum as the third choice; feet are reported as metres divided by 0.3048. Patch cords are counted separately as drops x patch cords per drop, because they are bought as assemblies rather than cut from the box. Inputs are refused outside 1 to 1000 drops, 0.5 to 150 m average run, 0 to 100 m riser, 0 to 50 percent slack and 0 to 4 patch cords per drop, drops and patch cords must be whole numbers, and decimal commas are accepted. The page does not survey a building, choose a cable category, check conduit or tray fill or bend radius, allow for waste from failed pulls, or know a manufacturer's actual box length; the average run and the slack allowance are site assumptions the user supplies. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Structured cabling: a structured cabling system runs horizontal cabling from each outlet to a telecommunications room, so a drop needs both a horizontal run and any riser distance to the room.
Wikipedia, Twisted pair: Ethernet cabling is sold on reels and in pull boxes in fixed lengths, which is why a job is ordered in whole boxes with slack for routing and termination.
Wikipedia, Foot (unit): since the 1959 international yard and pound agreement one foot is exactly 0.3048 metres, the conversion used for the 1000 ft and 500 ft box sizes.
